areas.name: Safe and Effective Care Environment
areas.description: The nurse promotes achievement of client outcomes by providing and directing nursing care that enhances the care delivery setting in order to protect clients and health care personnel.

areas.name: Health Promotion and Maintenance
areas.description: The nurse provides and directs nursing care of the client that incorporates the knowledge of expected growth and development principles, prevention and/or early detection of health problems, and strategies to achieve optimal health.

areas.name: Psychosocial Integrity
areas.description: The nurse provides and directs nursing care that promotes and supports the emotional, mental and social well-being of the client experiencing stressful events as well as clients with acute or chronic mental illness.

areas.name: Physiological Integrity
areas.description: The nurse promotes physical health and wellness by providing care and comfort, reducing client risk potential and managing health alterations.

integratedProcesses.name: Caring
integratedProcesses.description: The nurse and client interact in an atmosphere of mutual respect and trust. The nurse provides encouragement, hope, support and compassion to help achieve desired outcomes.

integratedProcesses.name: Clinical Judgment
integratedProcesses.description: The observed outcome of critical thinking and decision-making: an iterative, multi-step process that uses nursing knowledge to observe and assess presenting situations, identify a prioritized client concern and generate the best possible evidence-based solutions to deliver safe client care.

integratedProcesses.name: Communication and Documentation
integratedProcesses.description: Verbal and nonverbal interactions between the nurse and the client, significant others and the health care team, and the written or electronic records of client care that show adherence to standards of practice and accountability.

integratedProcesses.name: Culture and Spirituality
integratedProcesses.description: Interaction of the nurse and the client (individual, family or group) that recognizes and considers the client's self-identified, unique preferences for care, the applicable standard of care and legal considerations.

integratedProcesses.name: Nursing Process
integratedProcesses.description: A scientific, clinical reasoning approach to client care that includes assessment, analysis, planning, implementation and evaluation.

integratedProcesses.name: Teaching/Learning
integratedProcesses.description: Facilitation of the acquisition of knowledge, skills and abilities that promotes a change in behavior.

clinicalJudgmentSteps.name: Recognize cues
clinicalJudgmentSteps.description: Identify relevant and important information from different sources (e.g., medical history, vital signs).

clinicalJudgmentSteps.name: Analyze cues
clinicalJudgmentSteps.description: Organize and connect the recognized cues to the client's clinical presentation.

clinicalJudgmentSteps.name: Prioritize hypotheses
clinicalJudgmentSteps.description: Evaluate and prioritize hypotheses (urgency, likelihood, risk, difficulty, time constraints, etc.).

clinicalJudgmentSteps.name: Generate solutions
clinicalJudgmentSteps.description: Identify expected outcomes and use hypotheses to define a set of interventions for the expected outcomes.

clinicalJudgmentSteps.name: Take action
clinicalJudgmentSteps.description: Implement the solution(s) that address the highest priority.

clinicalJudgmentSteps.name: Evaluate outcomes
clinicalJudgmentSteps.description: Compare observed outcomes to expected outcomes.
